note: HAND-AUTHORED, not model output. Written from the deterministic synthesis input of the AI Coach scenario after the customer evidence was approved (as-of 2026-10-01). Evidence ids are symbolic selectors resolved against the request. Claim c7 is an INJECTED causal overclaim (typed causal, written as a causal statement about observational evidence): the validators reclassify its type, the Reviewer fixture flags it.

claims.text: Users with an ai_coach_session show 46.0% D90 retention against 22.9% for all other users, a difference of +23.0% (95% CI +21.7% to +24.4%) in an observational comparison.
The comparison is not randomised, so the difference may reflect which users adopt the coach rather than the coach itself.
The AI Coach holdout shows +0.293 workouts (95% CI +0.118 to +0.469) but its sample-ratio check failed, so its allocation cannot be trusted.
706 relevant feedback mentions describe the AI Coach as helpful for staying on track.
113 relevant feedback mentions describe the AI Coach as generic or as ignoring what the customer told it.
128 relevant feedback mentions describe the AI Coach as acceptable without a clear benefit.
The higher D90 retention among AI Coach users is caused by the coach itself.
The retention difference has a similar size within each engagement style, so the aggregate does not appear to hide a reversal.

uncertainties.text: The observational comparison cannot separate the effect of the coach from prior engagement.
The holdout experiment has a failed sample-ratio check.

gaps.text: No financial evidence exists for the cost of the coach per retained user.

sections.summary: Users of the AI Coach retain better at 90 days in an observational comparison [[c1]]. The only experiment has a failed sample-ratio check [[c3]]. Customer feedback is mixed [[c4]] [[c5]].
sections.supporting: The comparison shows a higher retention among coach users [[c1]]. Many feedback mentions describe the coach as helpful [[c4]].
sections.contradicting: Some feedback mentions describe the coach as generic or as ignoring the customer [[c5]].
sections.uncertainty: The comparison is observational [[c2]]. The holdout allocation cannot be trusted [[c3]].
